Alexander Weber''' (born December 29, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Karşıyaka Basket]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]], and spent three years in the [[NBA]]. ==High school career== Weber attended [[Great Bridge High School]] where he averaged 17 points, eight rebounds, five assists and four steals per game as a senior, earning the All-Southeastern District Defensive Player of the Year award during his junior and senior seasons.{{cite web|title=Briante Weber Bio|url=http://www.vcuathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2014-15/bios/weber_briante_lsnw|website=VCUAthletics.com|access-date=March 11, 2016|archive-date=June 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617010724/http://vcuathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2014-15/bios/weber_briante_lsnw|url-status=dead}} ==College career== In his college career with the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]], he was designated to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Defensive Team on multiple occasions, and also earned the title as the conference's Defensive Player of the Year for three straight seasons. He led the nation in [[steal (basketball)|steals]] through his junior season in [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14]] with a 3.46 average.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} On January 31, 2015, Weber's college career ended when he tore his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] in a loss to rival [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]]. Weber was only 12 steals away from becoming the NCAA's all-time career leader.{{cite web|last=Parrish|first=Gary|title=VCU's Briante Weber out for season with knee injury|work=CBSSports.com|date=January 31, 2015|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25014178/vcus-briante-weber-out-for-season-with-knee-injury|access-date=February 1, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2015–2016)=== Weber went undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], likely due to him still recovering from his ACL tear.{{cite web|title=VCU Basketball: Graham and Weber go undrafted|work=ISportsWeb.com|date=June 27, 2015|url=http://isportsweb.com/2015/06/27/vcu-basketball-graham-and-weber-go-undrafted/|access-date=June 27, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160514225753/http://isportsweb.com/2015/06/27/vcu-basketball-graham-and-weber-go-undrafted/|archive-date=May 14, 2016|url-status=dead}} He later attempted to join the [[Miami Heat]] for training camp but was unable to pass his physical due to the knee injury.{{cite web|title=Briante Weber's deal with the Heat is off the table|work=Sportando.com|date=September 11, 2015|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/175644/briante-weber-s-deal-with-the-heat-is-off-the-table.html|access-date=September 11, 2015}} He ultimately signed with the Heat on October 19, 2015,{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-briante-weber|title=Heat Signs Briante Weber|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 19, 2015|access-date=October 19, 2015}}{{cite news|last=Winderman|first=Ira|title=Heat cut Hawkins, add Weber in moves related to D-League affiliate|date=October 19, 2015|newspaper=South Florida Sun Sentinel|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/sfl-miami-heat-briante-weber-s101915-story.html|access-date=October 19, 2015}} but was waived five days later.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-requests-waivers|title=HEAT Waive Five Players|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 24, 2015|access-date=October 24, 2015}}{{cite news|last=Winderman|first=Ira|title=Heat cut five, roster down to 15-player regular-season limit|date=October 24, 2015|newspaper=South Florida Sun Sentinel|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/sfl-miami-heat-nba-roster-s102415-story.html|access-date=October 24, 2015}} On November 2, Weber was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Heat.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065971|title=Skyforce Announces 2015–16 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 2, 2015|access-date=November 4, 2015}} He missed the first month of the 2015–16 season due to the knee injury, making his debut for the Skyforce during the D-League Showcase on January 7, 2016.{{cite web|last=Peters|first=Dan|url=https://espn991.com/rebuilding-a-defensive-presence-in-skyforce-guard-briante-weber/|title=Rebuilding a Defensive Presence in Skyforce Guard Briante Weber|work=espn991.com|date=January 25, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}} He slowly built up his confidence and received more game time throughout January, scoring in double figures in five straight games between January 22 and February 3. On February 23, he recorded a triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a win over the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite web|last=Peters|first=Dan|url=https://espn991.com/skyforce-guard-briante-weber-earns-call-up-to-memphis/|title=Skyforce Guard Briante Weber Earns Call-Up to Memphis|work=espn991.com|date=March 9,
